host_orange.Mass (M-sun): WEAK -- INFERRED, equal-mass assumption. GJ 4113 is a twin SB2 (Marcussen & Albrecht 2023, AJ 165, 266 (arXiv:2305.08623), Sect. 4.5; Stefansson et al. 2025, AJ 169, 107 (arXiv:2410.05654), Table 4) with no published component mass. Blend Ks = 7.339 (2MASS J19333940+3931372), parallax 57.5696 mas (Gaia DR3 nss_two_body_orbit) -> M_Ks = 6.140; the Mann et al. 2019, ApJ 871, 63 (arXiv:1811.06938) M_Ks relation (n = 5, no [Fe/H] term) gives 0.418 Msun for it as one star (Stefansson et al.'s single-star 0.42 +/- 0.02, reproduced). Split equally, each component is 0.753 mag fainter, M_Ks = 6.893 -> 0.304 Msun. Relation scatter ~2%; valid for M_Ks 4-11, main-sequence stars. Marcussen & Albrecht's flux ratio of ~0.85 instead of 1 gives 0.316 + 0.291. Their working assumption, M1 = M2 = 0.47 Msun (Gaia DR3 binary_masses M1, the Systems row's value), is a mass for the blend's light and is not used here.
host_orange.Luminosity (L-sun): WEAK -- INFERRED: half the Systems row's 0.02484 Lsun, which is the pair's combined light, on the equal-mass assumption (see the Mass cell). Cifuentes et al. 2025 (A&A 693, A228) give 0.02593 Lsun for the unresolved pair.

values.Role in system: companion (SB2 secondary of GJ 4113; Marcussen & Albrecht 2023, AJ 165, 266)
values.Star data source: INFERRED, all of it: the unresolved SB2 secondary, assumed equal to A (Marcussen & Albrecht 2023 call it a twin binary, flux ratio ~0.85). Class and Teff are the blend's; mass and L as on A's row. The names A and B are this workbook's, not a catalogue's.
values.Kinematics source: none of its own: unresolved, shares GJ 4113's Gaia entry
values.Orbit source: Gaia DR3 nss_two_body_orbit (Orbital) for 2052469973468984192: P = 209.3157 +/- 0.74 d, e = 0.4698 +/- 0.044. This is the photocentre orbit that Gaia-ASOI-054 was read from; Marcussen & Albrecht 2023, AJ 165, 266 (arXiv:2305.08623) (Sect. 4.5) and Stefansson et al. 2025, AJ 169, 107 (arXiv:2410.05654) (Table 4, G-ASOI-54) find the star an SB2, so it is the binary's orbit. Neither paper fits an orbit of its own.
values.Separation source: COMPUTED here, not published: Kepler III on Gaia DR3's P = 209.3157 d and the inferred total mass 0.608 Msun (2 x 0.304). Orange; see cell note.

sp_paragraph: GJ 4113 (Ross 1063), a twin SB2: Marcussen & Albrecht 2023, AJ 165, 266 (arXiv:2305.08623), Sect. 4.5 and Table 1 (two FIES spectra, flux ratio ~0.85, M1 = M2 = 0.47 Msun ASSUMED); Stefansson et al. 2025, AJ 169, 107 (arXiv:2410.05654), Table 4 (SB2; 0.42 +/- 0.02 Msun as one star). Neither gives K1/K2, a mass ratio or an orbit. ORBIT: Gaia DR3 nss_two_body_orbit, P 209.3157 d, e 0.4698. INFERRED (orange): each star's mass 0.304 Msun, from the blend's 2MASS Ks 7.339 and parallax 57.5696 mas (M_Ks 6.140), split equally, through the Mann et al. 2019, ApJ 871, 63 (arXiv:1811.06938) M_Ks relation, n = 5, no [Fe/H] term (coefficients -0.642, -0.208, -0.000843, 0.00787, 0.000142, -0.000213; zero point 7.5; scatter 2.0%; valid 4 < M_Ks < 11, main-sequence, -0.6 < [Fe/H] < +0.4); as one star it gives 0.418, Stefansson et al.'s value. Each star's L 0.01242 Lsun = half the Systems row's 0.02484. Separation 0.584 au = (P^2 M)^(1/3). CONFIDENCE: LOW for the masses and the separation (no component is measured); the period is Gaia's. HOW TO VERIFY: IRSA fp_psc for the Ks, the Gaia archive for the orbit, Mann et al.'s Table 6 for the coefficients; data/refuted_pairs/add_pairs.py recomputes all of it.

Gaia DR3 nss_two_body_orbit has the same pair at P = 253.48 d, e = 0.134 (the orbit Gaia-ASOI-037 was read from); the paper finds the periods and eccentricities agree and the angles differ by 2.5-7.4 sigma.

sp_paragraph: APM 89 AB (APMPM J0710-5704, WDS 07096-5704 TSN 140): Vrijmoet et al. 2026, AJ 171, 186 (arXiv:2601.18905), Table 4: P 0.69778 +/- 0.00274 yr, a 0.0342 +/- 0.0011 arcsec, e 0.1373 +/- 0.0275, Mtot 0.409 +/- 0.040 Msun; first resolved in Vrijmoet et al. 2022, AJ 163, 178 (arXiv:2202.04688) (Delta I 0.1 mag). The paper does not discuss the planet candidate. INFERRED (orange): each star's mass 0.2045 Msun = Mtot / 2 and L 0.00422 Lsun = half the Systems row's 0.00844, on the near-equal pair; separation 0.584 au = a / Gaia DR3 parallax 58.5739 mas, arithmetic on published values (Kepler III with Mtot returns P = 0.698 yr). CONFIDENCE: HIGH for the orbit's period and size (speckle and Gaia agree), MEDIUM for the equal split. HOW TO VERIFY: the paper's Table 4; the WDS summary line for 07096-5704; data/refuted_pairs/add_pairs.py.
